newsitem.title: UK: Players pull back from copper options after spike.
newsitem.headline: Players pull back from copper options after spike.

text.p: A spike in copper prices to 2-1/2-month highs on Friday pushed up LME option volatilities and wary dealers said they were backing off from the market.
"The vols are definitely higher and the spreads are wider, but no-one is really quoting anything," one dealer said.
He estimated implied volatilities for December at-the-money options at 30.00/35.00 percent up from about 28.00/31.00 percent last week.
January was put at at 30.00/34.00 percent, also up several points on the week.
"No one is prepared to sell options, there are too many unknowns for them to go shorter than they already may be," another dealer said.
Delta covering helped Friday's price spike, with open interest on December LME options centred on the $2,100 strike at 2,044 lots at the close of business on Wednesday.
There was expected to be additional exposure on the OTC market.
"A lot of the dealers are short of these strikes. Every time the market looks like it is going to break up again there's panic short-covering," a dealer said.
Before Friday's action, the market had seen good two-way business in copper on upside calls, leaving volatilities only slightly firmer.
"Any selling has been more from speculative customers rather than market makers trying to do anything with their positions," a dealer said.
Strikes in play were $2,100 to $2,200 for December through May 1997.
Some of the buying was thought to have been from dealers who had been short Asian options for November and were covering with LME December options.
One dealer said producers were still looking for downside protection with puts for 1998 and 1999, but finding it difficult to find grantors.
"The problem is the market at these prices is not going to want to see puts because that's what hurt them the most before," one said.
Plunging prices in the wake of the Sumitomo scandal in June left many option grantors with large losses.
Aluminium volatilites eased as prices consolidated and selling came into the market, dealers said.
"We've seen some granting of $1,400/25 for the first quarter and we're seeing some 1400 calls and puts being sold for December over the last couple of days," a dealer said.
Implied volatilities for December at-the-money options were indicated at 19.00/22.00 percent, down about 1.5 to 2.0 percentage points on the week.
First quarter volatilties were pegged at 19.25/21.00 percent, down slightly.
Volatilties eased in nickel due to a few sellers impacting a thin market, dealers said.
December implied volatilities fell to 22.00/26.00 percent, down about five points on the week.
